ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the four corners of the rectangular paper $ABCD$ are folded inward to precisely form a quadrilateral $EFGH$ with no gaps and no overlaps. If $EH=3$ and $EF=4$, what is the length of side $BC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} We have $\because \angle HEM=\angle AEH$ and $\angle BEF=\angle FEM$, \\
$\therefore \angle HEF=\angle HEM+\angle FEM=\frac{1}{2}\times 180^\circ=90^\circ$, \\
Similarly, we find: $\angle EHG=\angle HGF=\angle EFG=90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ Quadrilateral $EFGH$ is a rectangle, \\
$\therefore GH=EF$ and $GH\parallel EF$, \\
$\therefore \angle GHN=\angle EFM$, \\
In $\triangle GHN$ and $\triangle EFM$ we have\\
$\left\lbrace\begin{array}{l}
\angle GNH=\angle EMF\\
\angle NHG=\angle MFE\\
HG=EF
\end{array}\right.$, \\
$\therefore \triangle GHN\cong \triangle EFM(AAS)$, \\
$\therefore HN=MF=HD$, \\
$\therefore AD=AH+HD=HM+MF=HF$, \\
$HF=\sqrt{EH^2+EF^2}=\sqrt{3^2+4^2}=5$, \\
$\therefore BC=AD=\boxed{5}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the outer boundary is the dashed rectangle ABCD, with A at the upper left, B at the lower left, C at the lower right, and D at the upper right. Point E is located on the left side AB, H is located on the upper side AD, G is located on the right side CD, and F is located on the lower side BC. After the four corners are folded inward, the internal quadrilateral EFGH is formed; the solid-line sides are EH, HG, GF, and FE. The seams after the internal folding can also be seen in the figure, where the left seam connects from E to point M on HF, and the right seam connects from G to point N on HF. Reasoning: Folding is mirror symmetry, so crease EH bisects the angle between the original side EA and the folded line EM, hence ∠HEM = ∠AEH; crease EF bisects the angle between the original side EB and the folded line EM, hence ∠BEF = ∠FEM. Since A, E, B are collinear, ∠AEB = 180°, so ∠HEF = ∠HEM + ∠FEM = 1/2 × 180° = 90°. Similarly, at H, G, and F, we also obtain ∠EHG = ∠HGF = ∠EFG = 90°, therefore EFGH is a rectangle. Thus GH = EF, and GH ∥ EF. Compare △GHN and △EFM: from the parallel relationship and the corresponding seams on HF in the figure, the corresponding angles are equal, and GH = EF, so △GHN ≅ △EFM (AAS). Therefore HN = MF. Also by folding symmetry, D folds to N, so HD = HN; A folds to M, so AH = HM. Thus AD = AH + HD = HM + MF = HF. In rectangle ABCD, BC = AD, so BC = HF. Since EFGH is a rectangle, HF is its diagonal, EH = 3, EF = 4, so HF = sqrt(3^2 + 4^2) = 5. Therefore BC = 5.

method.method_draft: Use angle-bisecting/reflection facts from the folds, then a triangle congruence. First read from the figure that E lies on AB, H on AD, G on CD, F on BC, and the folds are along EH, HG, GF, FE. Let the folded images of the relevant rectangle corners lie on the internal seams, with M on HF near the left folds and N on HF near the right folds as in the diagram. Because a fold line is the perpendicular bisector/angle mirror between the original corner and its image, EH bisects the angle between EA and EM, and EF bisects the angle between EB and EM. Since A,E,B are collinear, these two half-angles add to 90 degrees, so angle HEF is 90 degrees. Repeat at the other three sides to show all angles of EFGH are right angles, hence EFGH is a rectangle. Then GH = EF and GH is parallel to EF. Compare triangles GHN and EFM: they have corresponding right/parallel-line angles equal and hypotenuse/side GH = EF, so they are congruent by AAS. Therefore HN = MF, and by reflection HD = HN while AH = HM. Thus AD = AH + HD = HM + MF = HF. Since ABCD is a rectangle, BC = AD. Finally compute the diagonal of rectangle EFGH: HF = sqrt(EH^2 + EF^2) = sqrt(3^2 + 4^2) = 5, so BC = 5.

method.method_draft: Use an unfolding/path-length interpretation. From the picture, regard EFGH as the hole-free folded image of the four corner triangles, with the original top side AD split at H into AH and HD. First prove EFGH is a rectangle using the same mirror-angle observation from the folds: at E, the folded images of corners A and B meet without overlap, so the two reflected half-angles sum to half of the straight angle AEB, giving angle HEF = 90 degrees; similarly the other corners are right angles. Now unfold only the portions adjacent to the top side AD into the folded figure: folding across EH sends segment AH to an equal segment HM on the internal diagonal from H toward F, while folding across HG sends segment HD to an equal segment whose corresponding length can be matched to the remaining part MF of the same diagonal because the no-gap tiling of the folded rectangle pairs the right/top flap with the lower/left flap along parallel sides of rectangle EFGH. raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, the four corners of the rectangular paper $ABCD$ are folded inward to form a quadrilateral $EFGH$ with no gaps and no overlaps. If $EH=3$ and $EF=4$, what is the length of side $BC$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} We have $\because \angle HEM=\angle AEH$ and $\angle BEF=\angle FEM$, \\
$\therefore \angle HEF=\angle HEM+\angle FEM=\frac{1}{2}\times 180^\circ=90^\circ$, \\
Similarly, we find: $\angle EHG=\angle HGF=\angle EFG=90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ Quadrilateral $EFGH$ is a rectangle, \\
$\therefore GH=EF$ and $GH\parallel EF$, \\
$\therefore \angle GHN=\angle EFM$, \\
In $\triangle GHN$ and $\triangle EFM$ we have\\
$\left\lbrace\begin{array}{l}
\angle GNH=\angle EMF\\
\angle NHG=\angle MFE\\
HG=EF
\end{array}\right.$, \\
$\therefore \triangle GHN\cong \triangle EFM(AAS)$, \\
$\therefore HN=MF=HD$, \\
$\therefore AD=AH+HD=HM+MF=HF$, \\
$HF=\sqrt{EH^2+EF^2}=\sqrt{3^2+4^2}=5$, \\
$\therefore BC=AD=\boxed{5}$.
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the outer boundary is the dashed rectangle ABCD, with A at the upper left, B at the lower left, C at the lower right, and D at the upper right. Point E is located on the left side AB, H is located on the upper side AD, G is located on the right side CD, and F is located on the lower side BC. After the four corners are folded inward, the internal quadrilateral EFGH is formed; the solid-line sides are EH, HG, GF, and FE. The seams after the internal folding can also be seen in the figure, where the left seam connects from E to point M on HF, and the right seam connects from G to point N on HF. Reasoning: Folding is mirror symmetry, so crease EH bisects the angle between the original side EA and the folded line EM, hence ∠HEM = ∠AEH; crease EF bisects the angle between the original side EB and the folded line EM, hence ∠BEF = ∠FEM. Since A, E, B are collinear, ∠AEB = 180°, so ∠HEF = ∠HEM + ∠FEM = 1/2 × 180° = 90°. Similarly, at H, G, and F, we also obtain ∠EHG = ∠HGF = ∠EFG = 90°, therefore EFGH is a rectangle. Thus GH = EF, and GH ∥ EF. Compare △GHN and △EFM: from the parallel relationship and the corresponding seams on HF in the figure, the corresponding angles are equal, and GH = EF, so △GHN ≅ △EFM (AAS). Therefore HN = MF. Also by folding symmetry, D folds to N, so HD = HN; A folds to M, so AH = HM. Thus AD = AH + HD = HM + MF = HF. In rectangle ABCD, BC = AD, so BC = HF. Since EFGH is a rectangle, HF is its diagonal, EH = 3, EF = 4, so HF = sqrt(3^2 + 4^2) = 5. Therefore BC = 5.
